cold_email.subject: Interest in Educator / Empire Mall — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear lululemon Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Educator / Empire Mall opportunity with lululemon at lululemon.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Research Subject Protection Analyst I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Subject Protection Analyst I opportunity with Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center at Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.body:
Dear Remington Hospitality Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Human Resources Coordinator - SHERATON PHILADELPHIA opportunity with Remington Hospitality at Remington Hospitality.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.body:
Dear Labcorp Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Research Assistant (Study Tech)-Animal Operations opportunity with Labcorp at Labcorp.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Culture Laboratory Technician I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear HuFriedyGroup Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Culture Laboratory Technician I opportunity with HuFriedyGroup at HuFriedyGroup.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Program Assistant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Children's National Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Program Assistant opportunity with Children's National Hospital at Children's National Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Volunteer Program Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Broadmead, Inc. Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Volunteer Program Coordinator opportunity with Broadmead, Inc. at Broadmead, Inc..

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

Dear Applied Medical Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the AppliedKids Infant-Toddler Teacher (12ECE Units & 3 Infant-Toddler Units) opportunity with Applied Medical at Applied Medical.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Human Resources Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Stanford University Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Human Resources Coordinator opportunity with Stanford University at Stanford University.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Research Coordinator I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Fred Hutch Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Research Coordinator I opportunity with Fred Hutch at Fred Hutch.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Clinical Research Assistant — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Brown University Health Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Clinical Research Assistant opportunity with Brown University Health at Brown University Health.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Career Services Coordinator opportunity with Aviation Institute of Maintenance at Aviation Institute of Maintenance.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in 2027 University Graduate - Machine Learning Engineer — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Adobe Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the 2027 University Graduate - Machine Learning Engineer opportunity with Adobe at Adobe.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Quality Lab Technician - 1st Shift — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Baxter International Inc. Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Quality Lab Technician - 1st Shift opportunity with Baxter International Inc. at Baxter International Inc..

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator - Banfield of Charlotte University — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator - Banfield of Charlotte University opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator (Full Time): Regency 0299 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator (Full Time): Regency 0299 opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator - 001085 — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator - 001085 opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

cold_email.subject: Interest in Client Service Coordinator - Brier Creek Part-time — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Banfield Pet Hospital Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Client Service Coordinator - Brier Creek Part-time opportunity with Banfield Pet Hospital at Banfield Pet Hospital.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Process Engineer II
jobs.description: What if the work you did every day could impact the lives of people you know? Or all of humanity? At Illumina, we are expanding access to genomic technology to realize health equity for billions of people around the world. Our efforts enable life-changing discoveries that are transforming human health through the early detection and diagnosis of diseases and new treatment options for patients. Working at Illumina means being part of something bigger than yourself. Every person, in every role, has the opportunity to make a difference. Surrounded by extraordinary people, inspiring leaders, and world changing projects, you will do more and become more than you ever thought possible. You are the engineer Illumina is looking for. In your future role at the Madison site of the global leader in genetic sequencing, you will be part of the Engineering Services team providing process-focused engineering support for the equipment and systems producing the enzymes that fuel Illumina’s sequencing and array-based solutions. You will drive process performance through process development and design, data-driven troubleshooting, process capability assessment, yield improvement, scalable equipment solutions, process control strategy, and product and technical transfer from development through manufacturing implementation. You will support fermentation vessels, purification systems, heat treatment equipment, solids conveyance, centrifuges, chromatography instruments, cold storage, analytical equipment, and emerging platform projects. You will contribute to a self-directed, diverse team by improving process capabilities, strengthening equipment reliability, enabling scale-up readiness, and applying statistical and engineering methods to sustain control. We want your curiosity, creative problem solving, communication confidence, and drive to execute. Responsibilities Partner with cross-functional teams and vendors to support the design, troubleshooting, and improvement of manufacturing and laboratory systems, including fermentation, purification, PHT, solids conveyance, centrifugation, chromatography, cold storage, and analytical equipment. Apply process engineering principles to develop, optimize, and scale manufacturing processes and equipment using lean, Six Sigma, JMP, advanced Excel analytics, regression, DOE, statistical process control, and other data-driven methods. Use statistical analysis and engineering judgment to evaluate process performance, identify risks, improve efficiency, strengthen business continuity, and recommend maintenance, CIP, spare parts, and reliability strategies for critical manufacturing systems. Write, review, and manage engineering reports, protocols, user requirement specifications, maintenance work instructions, and technical documentation that support process design, equipment qualification, process control, and scale-up decisions. Incorporate quality, validation, and regulatory compliance requirements into system design, process engineering, equipment support, and continuous improvement activities. Develop specifications, feasibility assessments, and supporting engineering documents for scalable equipment layouts, system design, process design, qualification, and project implementation. Lead and contribute to cross-functional projects that align local, national, and international teams on process strategy, scale-up needs, equipment capability, and data-driven process improvement. Serve as a visible technical resource by mentoring supporting engineers, communicating process and system design recommendations clearly, and contributing to team culture through ownership and collaborative problem solving. Minimum Requirements: B.S. degree in Chemical Engineering or equivalent technical training/experience 2+ years relevant engineering experience. Experience in applying statistical tools, advanced Excel analytics, JMP, regression, DOE, and statistical process control to engineering reports, business cases, and process improvement decisions. Demonstrated ownership of complex, ambiguous technical work, including independent execution, high-quality documentation, and follow-through on cross-functional engineering commitments. Desire to grow toward a Senior Engineer role by leading complex cross-functional projects from concept through implementation, deepening unit operations expertise, mentoring others, and strengthening operator collaboration. The estimated base salary range for the Process Engineer II role based in the United States of America is: $76,500 - $114,700. Should the level or location of the role change during the hiring process, the applicable base pay range may be updated accordingly. The range reflects long‑term growth in the role; therefore, most candidates are hired between the minimum and middle of the range. Placement depends on experience, skills, location, and internal equity. Additionally, all employees are eligible for one of our variable cash programs (bonus or commission) and eligible roles may receive equity as part of the compensation package. We offer a wide range of benefits as innovative as our work, including access to genomics sequencing, family planning, health/dental/vision, retirement benefits, and paid time off. We are a company deeply rooted in belonging, promoting an inclusive environment where employees feel valued and empowered to contribute to our mission. Built on a strong foundation, Illumina has always prioritized openness, collaboration, and seeking alternative perspectives to propel innovation in genomics. We are proud to confirm a zero-net gap in pay, regardless of gender, ethnicity, or race. We also have several Employee Resource Groups (ERG) that deliver career development experiences, increase cultural awareness, and offer opportunities to engage in social responsibility. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer committed to providing employment opportunity regardless of sex, race, creed, color, gender, religion, marital status, domestic partner status, age, national origin or ancestry, physical or mental disability, medical condition, sexual orientation, pregnancy, military or veteran status, citizenship status, and genetic information. Illumina conducts background checks on applicants for whom a conditional offer of employment has been made. Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with applicable local, state, and federal laws. Background check results may potentially result in the withdrawal of a conditional offer of employment. The background check process and any decisions made as a result shall be made in accordance with all applicable local, state, and federal laws. Illumina prohibits the use of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in the application and interview process. If you require accommodation to complete the application or interview process, please contact accommodations@illumina.com. To learn more, visit: https://www.dol.gov/ofccp/regs/compliance/posters/pdf/eeopost.pdf. The position will be posted until a final candidate is selected or the requisition has a sufficient number of qualified applicants. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

cold_email.subject: Interest in Process Engineer II — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Illumina Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Process Engineer II opportunity with Illumina at Illumina.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: POSITION TITLE: Manager, Software Engineering POSITION LOCATION: San Carlos, CA, Austin, TX, or Remote, USA POSITION SUMMARY: Natera is seeking a hands-on, self-motivated Engineering Manager to lead a global software development team in the women's health domain in a fast-growing biotech company. In this pivotal role, you will be at the forefront of cutting-edge research in the field of non-invasive prenatal testing, overseeing a team dedicated to advancing our revolutionary initiatives. Your responsibilities will encompass not only the development and direction of a distributed engineering workforce but also the orchestration of project management activities and the facilitation of clear and effective communication across all levels.This is not a pure people-management role. You will spend some amount of your time hands-on: writing code, reviewing merge requests, and testing alongside your team.We are looking for someone who pairs strong technical judgment with real care for people, is energized by change, and wants to make a direct impact on tests that families rely on. RESPONSIBILITIES: Lead Provide technical leadership for a software development team, US-based and international, to deliver high-quality software on time and on budget Lead technical design, architecture, and implementation strategy for the team's services and integrations Establish and model engineering best practices, including how AI tools are used safely in a regulated environment Build Write production code on the team's services, taking tickets yourself, especially on critical-path and cross-team work Review merge requests every week. Hold a high bar for correctness, test coverage, and maintainability, whether the code was written by hand or with AI assistance Contribute directly to testing: write and extend automated tests, verify changes before release, and help triage production issues Stay close enough to the code to make sound technical calls and credible estimates Lead AI Transformation Use AI coding assistants and agentic tools (for example Claude Code, GitHub, Cursor) in your own daily work, and coach your team to do the same Redesign the team's workflow around AI: AI-assisted ticket refinement and spec-driven development AI-assisted code review AI-generated tests automation of repetitive work Build a cross-functional team where developers and test engineers both build and verify, and no one verifies their own work Measure AI's impact against the team's own baseline (cycle time, lead time, quality, time from grooming to ready) and share what works with other teams Keep people accountable for AI-assisted work, so that it meets our review, traceability, validation, and compliance requirements Manage Manage multiple concurrent projects spanning product launches, platform migrations, and production support Identify project objectives, the scope of software deliverables, external dependencies, resources, risks, and a framework for the project activities Facilitate collaboration and resolve issues, evaluate project performance, bring projects to delivery, and act on the lessons learned Lead team meetings and Agile rituals such as stand-ups, retrospectives, planning sessions, and demos Nurture Guide the career development of team members and grow their technical, interpersonal, and AI skills Provide individual performance feedback focused on recognition of achievement and opportunities for growth Conduct 1:1s, performance evaluations, and more Recruit and hire strong, diverse talent Collaborate Build and maintain ongoing strong working relationships with stakeholders, focus on building effective communication channels Build and maintain strong working relationships with product management, laboratory operations, bioinformatics, clinical, and quality partners Effect change Provide feedback to management and initiate change to optimize software development processes with focus on quality, innovation, and efficient product delivery QUALIFICATIONS: BS or MS degree in Computer Science or equivalent experience 2+ years of proven track record of building and managing high performance engineering teams 5+ years of experience in software development using Java or similar languages Practical, daily experience with AI coding tools and agentic workflows, and experience helping a team adopt them Experience in and aptitude for leading remote teams Excellent verbal and written communication skills Strong analytical and problem-solving skills Passion for people management and mentorship Experience in biotech, diagnostics, healthcare, or another regulated industry a strong plus KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Proven record of managing highly effective engineering teams Willingness and ability to manage global teams across multiple time zones Focus on recruiting strong and diverse talent Strong experience mentoring developers and test engineers, seeking out opportunities and giving guidance so engineers grow and excel Excellent project management skills in Agile environments Experience building enterprise back-end services using Java/Spring Boot or similar Experience with distributed and event-driven systems such as Kafka, workflow orchestration such as Temporal, relational databases, and AWS Hands-on coding, design, architecture, and code-review skills Test automation experience, and a habit of building quality in rather than inspecting it in A track record of using AI to measurably improve a team's delivery, backed by data rather than anecdotes Sound judgment about where AI helps and where it needs guardrails: verification, security, patient data privacy, and validation of regulated software Ability to collaborate cross-functionally and communicate effectively with reports, peers, and stakeholders Initiative: a proactive approach to addressing issues and finding creative solutions A strong work ethic and the ability to work well under pressure and in stressful circumstances Experience with Next Generation Sequencing data, bioinformatics pipelines, or genomics workflow platforms is a plus Experience developing software in a regulated environment (e.g., CLIA/CAP, FDA design controls, 21 CFR Part 11) is a plus #LI-DNI The pay range is listed and actual compensation packages are based on a wide array of factors unique to each candidate, including but not limited to skill set, years & depth of experience, certifications and specific office location. This may differ in other locations due to cost of labor considerations. jobs.description: Bold thinkers, breakthrough makers: Join a team of curious minds who challenge the status quo, create what’s next in science and technology, and have the freedom to turn daring ideas into real breakthroughs. The Opportunity Join our Translational Oncology department as a Scientist 3 , where your technical precision and deep immunological expertise will bridge the gap between early discovery and life-changing clinical therapies. In this pivotal, lab-based role, you will serve as our go-to flow cytometry expert, thriving in a collaborative, fast-paced environment that empowers bold scientific inquiry. Advance Oncology Pipelines: Generate robust, reproducible data to propel novel oncology targets from exploratory discovery straight into clinical development. Lead Flow Cytometry Execution: Design, execute, and analyze highly complex flow cytometry experiments, acting as the primary technical subject matter expert for the team. Innovate Multicolor Panels: Build, optimize, and troubleshoot large, high-parameter multicolor flow cytometry panels to enable deep immunophenotyping. Master Low-Input Samples: Perform rigorous, meticulous analysis on challenging, scarce samples, specializing in low cell count workflows. Drive Cross-Functional Strategy: Partner seamlessly with diverse project teams, translating and presenting complex data insights to influence key strategic decisions. Execute In Vitro Assays: Maintain and manipulate both primary human/murine cells and established cell lines using rigorous cell culture techniques. Who you are You hold a PhD in Immunology, Oncology, or a closely related scientific discipline. You bring exceptional, hands-on mastery of advanced flow cytometry, with a proven track record of building and troubleshooting large multicolor panels. You possess demonstrated expertise in analyzing challenging, low-input/low cell count biological samples. You have a deep, foundational understanding of immunology and tumor biology. You are proficient in sterile cell culture techniques involving both primary cells and established cell lines. You are an adaptable, detail-oriented team player with strong communication skills who thrives when navigating shifting priorities. You have experience or are willing to develop in-vivo models. jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Life Sciences Research (Genetic Medicine)
jobs.location: Boston, MA; San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Thousands of rare genetic diseases have a known cause but no approved treatment. Advances in gene editing and oligonucleotide medicines have made it possible to design therapies for very small populations, sometimes for a single patient, but developing them remains slow and costly. Anthropic’s Life Sciences team is exploring how frontier AI, combined with deep drug development expertise and strong external partnerships, can help change that. We’re hiring a Technical Program Manager to bring structure and momentum to this work. jobs.description: Position Summary The Supervisor of the clinical laboratory is a member of the Operations Department whose role is to oversee employees' performance and serve as a liaison between employees and senior management to meet company goals and quality objectives. The supervisor is responsible for daily supervision of lab staff performing duties such as laboratory testing and data review. Duties include but are not limited to coaching, motivating, staffing, evaluating, and training staff. The supervisor works closely with the manager to ensure company and team goals are met while adhering to good manufacturing practices and CLIA/CAP guidelines. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES Provides direct supervision to professional individual contributors and/or skilled, support individual contributors Ensures production work is consistently completed according to department goals. Administers company policies that directly affect subordinate employees. Monitors team members to ensure adherence to SOPs and safety procedures Oversees training and development of all staff members Document nonconformances and all corrective actions taken when test systems deviate from the established performance specifications as needed. Escalates protocol deviation to lead/supervisor. Handles employee issues in collaboration with the department manager and Human Resources. Ensures alignment with team for reasoning behind instructions/processes and changes Plans and leads shift meetings. Meets regularly with individual team members to discuss goals and progress Go-to person when manager is not present. May assist lab team in day-to-day tasks Keeps team morale up and maintains professionalism of team members, including by acting as role model. jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The ChatGPT Finances team builds experiences that help people connect their financial accounts, understand their financial picture, and ask useful questions about their finances through ChatGPT. Our work spans account connectivity, data ingestion, dashboards, personalized insights, and conversational experiences. We collaborate across product, design, research, infrastructure, security, and data integrations to make complex financial information understandable and actionable. This is an early and ambitious product area with a substantial roadmap. We are looking for engineers who want to shape both the first user experiences and the durable systems required to earn and keep users’ trust. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for full-stack product engineers to build and scale ChatGPT Finances. You will own features across the stack—from polished frontend experiences to the APIs, services, and data models that power them. This role is well suited to engineers who combine strong product judgment with broad technical depth. You should care about how quickly users can understand their financial lives, how reliably data moves through the system, and how AI can answer financial questions in a grounded, transparent, and useful way. You will work closely with product, design, research, infrastructure, security, and data integration teams to take ideas from early prototypes to reliable production experiences. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL - Own full-stack product features from user experience and frontend implementation through backend services, data models, deployment, and observability. - Build polished, accessible, and performant interfaces for account connection, dashboards, insights, and conversational workflows. - Design APIs and backend systems that safely ingest, normalize, and serve financial data. - Build resilient integrations that handle synchronization, data freshness, partial failures, permissions, and user consent. - Bring new AI capabilities into production while prioritizing grounding, accuracy, transparency, and user control. - Establish architecture, performance standards, testing practices, and operational safeguards for a fast-growing product area. - Debug and improve complex behavior across client, server, infrastructure, and external integrations. - Use qualitative feedback, product metrics, and experiments to improve user outcomes without compromising clarity or trust. - Collaborate across disciplines to turn ambiguous product opportunities into simple, reliable experiences. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Have experience building and shipping full-stack consumer products in production. - Are comfortable working in a modern frontend stack and building the APIs and services behind it. - Care deeply about product craftsmanship, performance, accessibility, and details that affect the user experience. - Understand API design, data modeling, system reliability, and the tradeoffs involved in evolving production systems. - Can move effectively between frontend, backend, and product decisions rather than remaining in a narrow implementation area. - Have strong product judgment and can take a feature from a rough idea to a shipped, measurable outcome. - Work well in ambiguous, high-impact areas where the product and technical architecture are still taking shape. - Think carefully about privacy, security, reliability, and user trust when working with sensitive data. - Enjoy diagnosing problems across system boundaries and improving the underlying engineering foundations. - Are interested in AI-native interfaces and new ways to make complex personal information easier to understand. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS - Experience building backend services using languages and frameworks such as Python, Go, Node.js, or comparable technologies. - Experience with frontend development using React / Typescript, or Swift or Kotlin. - Experience operating consumer products or distributed systems at scale. - Experience with fintech, personal finance, banking, payments, investing, or sensitive-data domain. - Familiarity with authentication, identity, permissions, privacy, and secure data flows. - Experience building dashboards, data visualizations, or insight-oriented products. - Familiarity with observability, experimentation, product metrics, and iterative development. - Experience with applied AI, conversational interfaces, or systems that incorporate model-generated output. jobs.description: The Role: Moderna is seeking a Quality Control Stability Associate II to join our QC Stability team in Norwood, MA. This role will support the routine execution of GMP stability programs across clinical and commercial programs, ensuring activities are performed in accordance with established procedures, policies, and applicable GxP and GMP requirements. The individual will play an important role in maintaining the consistent, compliant, and efficient execution of QC Stability operations. Here’s What You’ll Do Performing day-to-day routine stability program operations, such as stability sample pulls, sample aliquoting, sample submissions to testing labs, set-downs, sample verifications, additional sample requests, and shipment preparations for external labs. Creating, maintaining, and assisting with stability scheduling ensuring stability sample pulls occur as scheduled and within defined timelines. Ensuring proper operation and functioning of stability controlled-temperature units and cold rooms within validated temperature ranges and loading patterns. Responding to notifications of out-of-range controlled-temperature units and cold rooms within scheduled working hours and escalating to QC Stability management. Ensuring proper handling of stability study materials and stability samples with attention to all material handling requirements in applicable procedures and protocols. Managing and stocking of QC lab supplies and consumables required for performing stability operations. Ensuring compliance with all lab safety requirements. Following all relevant GxP regulations, guidelines, and company policies to ensure compliance with regulatory and internal requirements. Executing tasks precisely as defined in internal guiding documents including but not limited to standard operating procedures (SOPs) and work instructions. Following Good Documentation Practices and Data Integrity requirements to ensure data, documentation, and records are completed and maintained for use by the business and available to support audits or inspections. Completing training in assigned required learning plan according to the defined timing and the prescribed requalification cadence. May support and/or participate in audits and regulatory inspections. Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications) Education: Bachelor’s degree in relevant scientific discipline Experience: 2-3 years in a GMP QC laboratory setting with focus on Stability (preferable in life science or equivalent) Minimum knowledge required: cGMPs, general laboratory safety Minimum skills required: Pipetting Proficiency with Microsoft Office Programs Familiarity with electronic databases (e.g. LIMS, SAP, eQMS, CMMS) Strong written and oral communication skills as well as organizational skills Our Working Model As we build our company, we have always believed that an in-person culture is critical to our success. This role is 100% onsite, reflecting the importance of being physically present to support the work, collaborate closely with colleagues, and contribute to our site-based operations. Working onsite enables real-time collaboration, strong team connections, direct mentorship, and the hands-on partnership needed to deliver our mission. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact. Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment. That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance. jobs.title: Manager Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs
jobs.description: POSITION SUMMARY: The Manager, Regulatory Affairs and Quality Assurance (Biologics) drives complex FDA regulatory submissions for biologic programs, from Phase 1 through marketing applications (BLA/NDA). At Natera, we move fast because there is a patient waiting for every test and treatment . In this role, you will build and own quality systems, translate executive strategy into compliant submissions, and provide regulatory guidance to ensure rapid product approvals. You will coordinate risk assessments balancing technical impact, patient safety, and regulatory compliance. PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES: Turn executive strategy, development priorities, and target product profiles into actionable regulatory plans and submissions. Apply in-depth knowledge of FDCA, PHS Act Section 351, 21 CFR, and FDA/ICH guidance to build submissions that meet current agency expectations. Guide cross-functional teams in preparation for pre-IND/INTERACT and FDA meeting requests (Type A/B/C/D, pre-BLA/NDA). Author and review CMC (Module 3), nonclinical (Modules 2.4/2.6, 4), or clinical (Modules 2.5/2.7, 5) components of regulatory submissions. Support RA leadership in maintaining INDs, including protocol amendments, safety reports, and change notifications. Prepare briefing materials, question strategies, and tracking minutes for FDA meetings. Draft technical responses to FDA information requests and clinical holds. Represent Regulatory Affairs on program teams to ensure deliverables meet regulatory requirements with the least-burdensome approaches. Own core quality system processes, including CAPA, nonconformance reports (NCRs), change control, and SOP management. Build and maintain agile quality systems that ensure compliance without slowing down our ability to deliver critical products. Support FDA and CDMO inspection readiness (PAI/PLI, BIMO) through mock inspections and document preparation. Manage and develop a team of quality and regulatory professionals as business needs require. QUALIFICATIONS: B.S., M.S., or equivalent in Life Sciences, Pharmacy, Chemistry, Biochemistry, or Engineering (experience may substitute for education). 5-8 years of biotech or pharma industry experience in regulatory affairs, including Phase 1 IND through marketing application. Biologics experience preferred. Hands-on experience with eCTD and FDA ESG submissions. Working knowledge of FDA biologics regulations (21 CFR Parts 11, 50, 56, 58, 210/211, 312, 600-610) and ICH guidelines. Direct experience managing CAPA, NCR, and change control in an electronic QMS. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Capable of operating independently and building structure where it is missing . Strong scientific writing and risk assessment skills, relying on evidence and data to make decisions . Clear, proactive communicator who adapts quickly to shifting priorities . Experience with CBER- or CDER-regulated biologics (monoclonal antibodies, recombinant proteins, cell/gene therapy). RAC certification or ASQ CQA/CQE is a plus. CDMO oversight and phase-appropriate GMP experience. jobs.title: GTM Strategy & Operations, Generalist
jobs.description: About the Team The GTM Strategy & Growth team drives the growth and evolution of our B2B business across products, customer segments, and routes to market. We partner closely with Product, Sales, Success, Data Science, Finance, and Marketing to define and execute go-to-market strategies for new product launches, commercialization models, customer growth initiatives, and market expansion opportunities. Our work sits at the intersection of product strategy, growth, and operations — shaping how we bring products to market, how we measure success, and how we scale adoption across customer segments. We operate across both strategic and highly operational domains, from defining long-term growth bets and commercial strategy to building launch plans, tracking performance, and driving cross-functional execution across the business. About the Role We’re looking for a strategic, hands-on individual contributor to join our GTM Strategy & Growth team and help shape how we grow and scale our B2B business across products, customer segments, and routes to market. This is a generalist role for someone who combines strong product intuition with thoughtful GTM strategy and can flex seamlessly between strategic thinking and operational execution. You’ll translate business priorities into clear growth strategies, operating plans, and cross-functional execution. Your work may span product launches, commercialization models, customer growth initiatives, market expansion, and the systems and processes that help the business scale. You should be highly analytical, comfortable working across a range of products and business problems, and experienced navigating complex cross-functional environments. Experience with technical or API-based products is valuable, but the most important qualities are strategic range, sound judgment, and the ability to turn customer, product, and market insights into practical recommendations and action. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. In this role, you will: - Drive go-to-market strategy across products, customer segments, and routes to market, partnering closely with Product and GTM leaders to shape growth priorities and commercialization approaches. - Develop goals, launch success metrics, and operating KPIs for new initiatives, and monitor performance in partnership with Data Science and Analytics teams. - Develop growth strategies and strategic bets across new products, capabilities, customer motions, and market opportunities. - Develop customer segmentation frameworks and tailored strategies for different customer profiles, industries, and stages of adoption. - Partner with Product teams to provide structured customer feedback, market insights, and prioritization input that informs product roadmap decisions. - Collaborate with Pricing, Finance, and Product teams to develop commercial models, packaging, and monetization strategies, ensuring downstream GTM execution aligns with the broader commercial strategy. - Conduct market, competitive, and customer research to identify whitespace opportunities and inform strategic decision-making. - Partner cross-functionally with Sales, Customer Success, Marketing, Product, Finance, and Operations to align on priorities and execute against business goals. - Analyze business performance and identify opportunities to improve GTM strategy and operating plans based on data, customer insights, and market dynamics. jobs.description: About the Team Join us at DoorDash, where our people are our most valuable asset. About the Role The DoorDash Architecture and Security team is looking for a Solutions Architect, Business Technology Security with demonstrated experience and knowledge in Workday Security. This role owns the strategy and design of Workday security architecture, and ensures it translates correctly into the custom, in-house tools and dashboards built downstream of it. This is a strategy and design-focused role so success here depends heavily on your ability to gather clear requirements, write them up well, and communicate design decisions to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. You will interact directly with senior leaders and cross-functional partners across DoorDash to capture requirements and design lasting, secure solutions that hold up across the full ecosystem. This role will report to the Sr. Manager, Architecture and Security. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Own the strategy and design of Workday’s security architecture — data models, security groups, domains, and business process security — that serves as DoorDash’s security source of truth for the People organization. Translate that architecture into clear requirements and design documentation that our build team can implement, and that downstream custom tools and dashboards can be built against safely. Review new or proposed custom tooling and downstream reporting needs to identify security touchpoints and data access implications before they’re built, advising on the right design approach. Partner with process owners to define data security policies, protocols, and procedures that protect sensitive HR data across Workday and downstream systems. Conduct regular audits and risk assessments across Workday and the tools and reporting layers downstream of it, maintaining a forward-looking security and data classification roadmap. Serve as the subject matter expert on security, data, and reporting capabilities and limitations, communicating trade-offs clearly to both build teams and non-technical business stakeholders. We’re excited about you because… You have 5-7 years of work experience in HRIS implementation and configuration, both domestic and international, with deep expertise in Workday Security. You have extensive experience with one or more Workday HCM modules (Core HCM, Reporting, Payroll, Time & Labor, Compensation, Talent Management, Absence Management) and understand how their security models interact. You are an excellent requirements writer — you can turn an ambiguous business or security need into a clear, detailed design or requirements document that another team can build from without having to guess your intent. You have experience translating Workday security and data architecture into requirements for downstream, custom-built tools and reporting systems. You have a BA/BS degree in a quantitative or business field, or equivalent work experience. You have excellent written and verbal communication skills, comfortable presenting design recommendations to senior stakeholders and handing off clear specs to a separate engineering or build team. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched. Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you. At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started. ROLE OVERVIEW Harvey is redefining what’s possible in legal work by combining cutting-edge AI with intuitive product experiences. As we scale rapidly and take on increasingly complex use cases, we’re expanding our Applied AI engineering team to accelerate our ability to ship fast, delight users, and build infrastructure that scales with us. As an Engineering Manager for Applied AI, you’ll lead teams of fullstack engineers building out new surfaces with specialized agentic workflows for lawyers and other professionals to use every day. You’ll lead 0->1 product builds that enable complex agentic workflows through elegant user interfaces. This role is equal parts product intuition and technical execution. You’ll be trusted to make fast, high-quality decisions, ship impactful features, and grow a team that embodies engineering excellence and AI-led software development. WHAT YOU HAVE - 3+ years of experience in a software engineering management role leading fullstack product engineering teams, preferably in high-growth environments. - 5+ years of experience as a fullstack or backend product engineer. - A track record of leading high-performing, engaged engineering teams. - Strong product sense and an instinct for balancing speed, quality, and user impact. - Experience with modern frontend frameworks (e.g. React) and backend systems (e.g. Python, Node, Go). - A plus: Exposure to AI-powered applications or complex internal tools.
